cards.a: SPAN mirrors traffic from one or more source interfaces (or VLANs) to a destination analyzer port for analysis. It is local to the same switch and one-way.

cards.q: What are the source, destination, and scope of a SPAN session?
cards.a: The source is an interface or VLAN, the destination is an analyzer/IDS port, direction can be rx/tx/both, and scope is a single local switch.

cards.q: What do the SPAN direction keywords rx, tx, and both mean?
cards.a: rx mirrors received traffic, tx mirrors transmitted traffic, and both mirrors traffic in both directions. Configure via monitor session 1 source ... rx/tx/both.

cards.q: How do SPAN, RSPAN, and ERSPAN differ in scope?
cards.a: SPAN is local to the same switch, RSPAN is remote via a VLAN, and ERSPAN is remote via IP/GRE.

cards.q: What commands build a SPAN session?
cards.a: monitor session N source interface Gi x/y (rx/tx/both) defines the source, monitor session N destination interface Gi a/b defines the analyzer, and monitor session N vlan X sets a VLAN source. Use no monitor session N to remove it.

cards.q: What are the limitations of SPAN?
cards.a: SPAN is local only with no routing, uses TCAM/session resources, can cause loops when mirroring VLANs, and mirroring everything can overload and drop traffic.

cards.q: How do you verify a SPAN session?
cards.a: Use show monitor session 1 or show monitor to check the configuration and confirm the session.

cards.q: A SPAN capture is empty; what is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: Likely a direction issue; check whether rx/tx/both is set correctly. Also confirm the destination session with show monitor.

cards.q: What is the classic exam trap about SPAN destinations?
cards.a: SPAN destinations are analyzer ports that are not routable like normal ports; SPAN itself does not route and is local only.

cards.q: What is the difference between local SPAN and remote RSPAN/ERSPAN?
cards.a: SPAN is local port mirroring on one switch; RSPAN and ERSPAN are remote and require separation (VLAN or IP/GRE), so remote mirroring cannot be done with plain local SPAN.
